newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo in Tanzania nickel/cobalt deal.
newsitem.headline: Anglo in Tanzania nickel/cobalt deal.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd announced on Monday it had signed an agreement with Canadian company Sutton Resources Ltd for the acquisition of a majority stake in a nickel and cobalt project in Tanzania.
Anglo said in a statement this deal follows a period of due diligence, evaluation and negotiations.

Anglo said it expects to contribute $27 million towards the development of the project in order to acquire a 60 percent shareholding in Kabanga Nickel Company, which holds the rights to the Kabanga Nickel-Cobalt Project.

In terms of the agreement, Anglo will undertake a programme of additional exploration drilling at the Kabanga Nickel-Cobalt Project in north-western Tanzania and will complete a feasibility study within a period of four years.

Robert Danchin, chairman of Anglo's New Mining Business Division, said he was optimistic that the programme of exploration and drilling, to be conducted over the next 18 months, would provide the necessary basis for the establishment of a mine and treatment facility at Kabanga.
"We are encouraged by the support given to the project by the Government of Tanzania and trust that this marks the beginning of a successful and mutually beneficial relationship," he said.
